$comment: Mission 1.66.2 Part G. The three sent questions, reassessed against the documentation found afterwards. The enquiry itself is not edited.
mission: 1.66.2 — ONYPHE Public Documentation Reconciliation & Configuration-Metadata Closure V1

the_enquiry_was_not_edited.why_it_may_not_be_edited: It was sent. A document that was sent and then altered is a record of something nobody received.

questions.what_the_public_documentation_added: Verbatim time-range function descriptions, a documented default sort, and a timestamp definition that names both a collection moment and last-observed tracking in one sentence.
questions.why_it_is_still_unresolved: None of it addresses the repeated-observation case. Four first-party pages were consulted specifically for it, including the write-up whose title names historical queries, and none states whether a second scan of the same service creates a document or updates one.
questions.was_asking_it_justified: Yes, and more strongly than before. The question was asked because the public documentation did not answer it; a directed search of the public documentation has now confirmed that it does not.

questions.$comment: Three subparts, kept apart, because collapsing them would let one answer stand for three.

subparts.subpart: is TCP/22 in the datascan set
subparts.basis: the published port list carries one section and it is headed for ctiscan; no datascan TCP section exists on that page

subparts.subpart: what the current datascan configuration is
subparts.basis: 500 ports from US/FR and the TOP 25 from SG/CN, quoted from the Data Refresh Rate page
subparts.what_is_not: the membership, which is what the question asks

subparts.subpart: is the configuration recorded against a date or a version
subparts.basis: the 2024 retrospective documents that port counts, cadence and scanner regions all changed
subparts.what_is_constrained: that the configuration MOVES, which was previously unknown and is now first-party established
subparts.what_is_not: which ports were in the set on any given date, which is still published nowhere
subparts.direction_of_the_finding: It makes the question more necessary rather than less. An unchanging configuration would not need to be dated.

questions.$comment: Three fields, classified independently, because one answered field is not three.
questions.what_the_public_documentation_added: The retention sentence re-read verbatim, confirming that it names the truncated field and does not name the removed ones, and the data model confirming that all five fields exist and what they mean.
questions.the_already_known_half_stays_known: That the raw response field is truncated rather than removed. Question 3 states it as known and declines to re-ask it, which is still the right shape.

summary.the_honest_reading: A twelve-document directed search of the provider's own public documentation moved no question to answered. That is not a wasted budget: it converts *we have not found it* into *we looked where it would be and it is not published*, which is what makes the enquiry worth having sent.
